solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Go wrong, putting last message into place the wrong way round

indicators.note: putting one thing somewhere sets it inside the other piece here
into says where the message goes: inside the reversed word for place
the word for place is written back to front before the insertion

parts.note: to put something is to place it
RIP, rest in peace, is the final message on a gravestone

explanation.surface: Someone botches a job by fitting a farewell note in backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' looks like a noun but is the verb, meaning to set something down; 'the wrong way round' turns that word back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip up is to stumble or make a mistake, the same idea as going wrong.

clue.text: Admonish salesperson on journey without purpose

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to rove is to wander with no fixed aim

explanation.surface: Telling off a travelling salesman who wanders about aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove someone is to scold or rebuke them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Group of friends have to abandon ship

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving letters behind, so they drop out of the word for have

parts.note: to have something is to possess it
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A band of friends must leave a sinking vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' removes SS from the end of POSSESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is informally a gang or crowd of mates, from the sheriff's band of helpers.

clue.text: Is son entertained by minister of religion most proper?

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a priest is a minister of religion
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A question whether a boy hosted by a clergyman is the most strait-laced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' means held inside: the pair of words lands after the clergyman's first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Prissiest is the superlative of prissy, fussily prim and respectable.

clue.text: Bit about disgrace when a whole lot of information is needed

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for bit is read backwards

parts.note: a tad is a small bit
to abase is to humiliate or disgrace

explanation.surface: A slight shame is felt whenever masses of facts are demanded.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is a large organised store of data held on a computer.

clue.text: What may not be seen on cloudy night persistently bothers sailor

definitions.text: What may not be seen on cloudy night

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow and trouble them relentlessly
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Something hidden on an overcast evening keeps pestering a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the Dog Star, is the brightest star in the sky, hidden when clouds cover it.

clue.text: Conservative in genuine move towards permanent peace

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits in the middle of the word for genuine

parts.note: genuine means true

explanation.surface: A Tory makes a sincere attempt at lasting peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is a ceasefire, a step that can lead on to a lasting settlement.

clue.text: However, two revolutionaries may be killed

parts.note: however means but
Che Guevara and a Red, a communist, are two revolutionaries side by side

explanation.surface: A warning that a pair of rebels could be executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two revolutionaries' supplies two names: CHE then RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchered means slaughtered brutally, a strong synonym for killed.

clue.text: Gentleman reportedly lavish, almost offering superfluity

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the title for a gentleman is said, not spelt

parts.note: sir is the title or address for a gentleman

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: plush means luxurious or lavish

explanation.surface: A man of means seems nearly extravagant in what he gives away.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR said in a non-rhotic accent gives SUR; 'almost' drops the H of PLUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an excess beyond what is needed, a superfluity.

clue.text: Part I played with smugness, being good enough

indicators.note: letters played with are toyed around into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor performs his role with self-satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass muster is to meet the required standard, as soldiers at an inspection.

clue.text: From what we hear, not all are flexible in this county

indicators.note: this tells the solver the phrase is spoken, not written

parts.note: if not all are flexible, then some are set, that is rigid

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that the people of a certain county are stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'some are set' runs together into the county name. SOMERSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an English county, in the West Country.

clue.text: Expire, no longer in good health

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
hale means healthy and strong

explanation.surface: To die, no longer being fit and well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expire' suggests death, but its literal sense is breathing out.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire is literally to breathe out, which is to exhale.

clue.text: Kind that may help angler catch fish

definitions.meaning: kind as an adjective: mild and tender

definitions.text: that may help angler catch fish
definitions.meaning: a maggot, a blowfly larva used as fishing bait

explanation.surface: Describing a sort of bait an angler might use.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle means kindly; as a noun it is an old name for a bait maggot.

clue.text: Excellent artist winning gold award?

definitions.meaning: excellent means first-rate, of the highest class

explanation.surface: Praise for a painter who takes first prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer means of the highest quality or social class, as the best things kept in the top drawer.

clue.text: New fir trees? Nothing for one to put new trees in!

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made fresh in another order
one thing put for another means replacing it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Planting a fresh batch of conifers in a bare plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts O in place of the I of FIR TREES, giving FORTREES, which 'New' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To reforest land is to plant it with trees again after clearance.

clue.text: Bigger monarch gaining pounds? One uses butter

indicators.note: gaining means taking something in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: fatter means bigger in girth
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A portly king putting on weight spreads butter on his bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is the verb in 'butter up', to flatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatterer butters people up, using praise to win favour.

clue.text: I must have moved slowly around — useless making creaking noise

indicators.note: the word for moved slowly goes around the letter

parts.note: crept means moved slowly and quietly
US is short for unserviceable, useless

explanation.surface: Someone shuffling about uselessly makes a creaking sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepitus is the medical term for a crackling or grating sound, as from joints.

clue.text: Relation suffers, lacking a particular vitamin

indicators.note: a word that suffers is knocked about, so its letters are rearranged
lacking means going without, so the letter is removed

explanation.surface: A family member falls ill for want of some vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes A from RELATION, and 'suffers' rearranges RELTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinol is vitamin A, the form found in animal foods.

clue.text: European region is upsetting the French over one area

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns a word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: les is French for the (plural)
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A disturbing complaint about the French presence in an area.
explanation.definitionFit: Silesia is a historical region of central Europe, now mostly in Poland.

clue.text: Press gently, penetrating muscles? That can bring feeling of anxiety

indicators.note: one piece penetrates the other, going into it

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles
to dab is to press lightly

explanation.surface: A light massage of the stomach muscles may cause nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The ABDABS (as in 'the screaming abdabs') is British slang for a fit of nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdabs is informal British slang for nervous agitation or dread.

clue.text: One may cover the eyes with boyfriend coming round

indicators.note: the boyfriend comes round, encircling the other piece

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend
and means together with

explanation.surface: A blindfold appears when a lover pays a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandeau is a narrow band of cloth, which can be worn over the eyes.

clue.text: Bone in the ear not right? Get excited

indicators.note: not means without, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: the stirrup, or stapes, is a small bone in the middle ear

explanation.surface: A painful ear makes someone agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up is to rouse or agitate, and so to get worked up.

clue.text: Forward types — people paid to keep quiet

indicators.note: to keep is to hold within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: pros are professionals, people paid for their work
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Pushy sorts are paid off to stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward types' suggests bold people; it means rugby forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the props are front-row forwards, so they are forward types.

clue.text: Party in the courtroom

parts.note: party here is not a celebration but one of the sides in a lawsuit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a festivity held in court; legally a party is a side in a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigant is a person involved in a lawsuit, a party to the action.

clue.text: One waited for move, the tiniest amount

parts.note: to go is to move
a dot is a tiny speck, the least amount

explanation.surface: Someone expected makes a slight movement.
explanation.walkthrough: In Beckett's play Waiting for Godot the title character never arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Godot is the absent figure the tramps wait for in Beckett's play.

clue.text: It can demonstrate laws centred on moving

definitions.text: It can demonstrate laws centred on moving

indicators.note: moving letters around puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A gadget that shows physical laws through motion.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is 'laws centred on'; the whole clue describes the desk toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Newton's cradle, with swinging steel balls, demonstrates conservation of momentum and energy.

clue.text: Novel about troubled lass, about a bounder ultimately getting one

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the shuffled girl goes round the other letters
a troubled girl is disturbed, so her letters are mixed
ultimately means at the end, picking the final letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A story of a distressed girl who comes to grief with a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges LASS to LSSA, and 'about#2' wraps it round A, R (from 'ultimately' on bounder) and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarissa is Samuel Richardson's eighteenth-century epistolary novel, whose heroine is ruined by the rake Lovelace.

clue.text: Driver finally taking a wrong turn from busy road?

definitions.text: Driver finally taking a wrong turn from busy road?

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word
a wrong turn here is the word turn in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A motorist turns off a congested main road.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the motorist's escape route.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat run is a minor side road that drivers use to dodge traffic on a busy main road.
